title: Snake game simulation
prompt:
Simulate a snake game on a board 8 columns wide and 6 rows tall. A cell is written (x, y), with x from 0 (left column) to 7 and y from 0 (top row) to 5. The snake starts with its head at (2, 2) and its body at (1, 2) and (0, 2), the last being its tail; it starts moving right. Food appears at the positions of this list, one at a time: (4, 2), (2, 2), (6, 4), (0, 5), (7, 0), (3, 3). At the start the food is at the first position of the list. When food is eaten, the new food is put at the next position of the list that is not occupied by the snake at that moment (the positions passed over are never used); if the list is used up, there is no more food.
The moves are the letters of `RRDLURLDDRDLLLLLLURDRR`, one step per letter, in order: U is up (y decreases), D down (y increases), R right, L left. A letter for the direction opposite to the snake's current direction is ignored, and the snake keeps moving in its current direction; any other letter becomes the current direction. In each step, the new head cell is the cell next to the head in the current direction, and the snake grows in this step if the new head cell holds food. The game ends at this step if the new head cell is outside the board, or is a cell of the snake other than its tail, or is the tail's cell while the snake grows in this step. (When the snake does not grow, its tail leaves its cell in the same step, so the head may move into the tail's cell.) When the game ends at a step, nothing of that step happens, and the remaining letters are ignored. Otherwise the head moves to the new cell, and:
- if the snake grows, all its other cells stay where they are, the food is eaten, and the next food appears;
- otherwise every other cell of the snake moves to the cell of the part in front of it, so the tail's old cell becomes empty. Then print `game over at move K` if the game ended at the K-th letter (counting from 1), or `all moves done` if it never ended; then `score S`, the number of foods eaten; then `length L`, the number of cells of the snake; then the board as 6 lines of 8 characters, top row first: `H` for the head, `o` for the other cells of the snake, `*` for the food, and `.` for an empty cell.

score 3
